chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Musa ibn Bakr said:

I said to Zurarah: Bukayr narrated to me from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'The paternal brothers and sisters, and those from both father and mother, are increased and decreased [in share] because they would not have a greater share than the paternal brothers and sisters if they were in their place.'
For Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: 'If a man dies leaving no child and he has a sister, then for her is half of what he left, and she inherits him if he has no child.'

He explains: 'He inherits all her wealth if she has no child.' So they gave to the one Allah specified for half, fully, and they aimed to give to the one Allah specified for all the wealth less than half, and the woman is never given a greater share than a man if he were in her place.'
He said, so Zurarah said: 'And this is established among our companions; they do not differ regarding it.'

key_terms.أَصْحَابِنَا: Our companions (referring to the Shia jurists/scholars)
key_terms.النِّصْفُ: Half (the specific share mentioned in the Quranic verse)
key_terms.الْأَخَوَاتِ لِلْأَبِ وَالْأُمِّ: Full sisters (sharing both father and mother)

ai.seo_question: How are the inheritance shares of paternal siblings determined in relation to full siblings according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the Shia jurisprudential principle of *al-awl* (adjustment) applied to paternal siblings (*akhawat lil-ab*) to ensure their share never exceeds that of full siblings, as derived from Surah An-Nisa 4:176. Zuraarah confirms this view is the consensus (*ijma'*) among the Shia scholars (*ashabuna*), distinguishing it from other schools by maintaining that the female sibling's share remains strictly half or less relative to the male, preventing any scenario where she inherits more than a male counterpart would in her place.
